description: CREATE PROCEDURE for SQL scripting procedures, asserted through SQL: each procedure is CALLed and both its RETURN VALUE and its SIDE EFFECTS are checked, and existence is read back through SHOW PROCEDURES LIKE, never through engine internals - so every assertion here holds against a live account too. Covers a procedure that UPDATEs by bind variable (and leaves the other row alone), one with NO parameters that DELETEs, a SCHEMA-QUALIFIED one where the body's BARE table name resolves in the procedure's HOME schema rather than the caller's, one with three parameters of three types, one with an IF / ELSE, one with a WHILE loop returning an OBJECT, and DROP PROCEDURE removing it from the listing. This is the invocation-side companion of scripting-create-procedure-listing, which covers the SHOW PROCEDURES listing. Converted 1:1 from scripting/CreateProcedureTest (now retired); the loop test asserted only that the rendered OBJECT CONTAINS 'count', '10' and 'completed', so the converted step pins the whole rendering.

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE data_rows (id INTEGER, label VARCHAR)
CREATE PROCEDURE update_data(id INTEGER, value VARCHAR) RETURNS VARCHAR AS 'BEGIN UPDATE data_rows SET label = :value WHERE id = :id; RETURN ''updated''; END'
SELECT id, label FROM data_rows ORDER BY id
CREATE PROCEDURE cleanup() RETURNS VARCHAR AS 'BEGIN DELETE FROM temp_table; RETURN ''cleaned''; END'
CREATE PROCEDURE my_schema.process_orders(order_id INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN RETURN (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM orders); END'
CREATE TABLE people (name VARCHAR, age INTEGER, active BOOLEAN)
CREATE PROCEDURE insert_record(name VARCHAR, age INTEGER, active BOOLEAN) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN INSERT INTO people (name, age, active) VALUES (:name, :age, :active); RETURN 1; END'
SELECT name, age, active FROM people
CREATE PROCEDURE test_proc(x INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN RETURN x * 2; END'
CREATE PROCEDURE proc1(x INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN RETURN x; END'
CREATE PROCEDURE proc2(x INTEGER, y INTEGER) RETURNS INTEGER AS 'BEGIN RETURN x + y; END'
CREATE TABLE test_table (id INTEGER, name VARCHAR)
CREATE PROCEDURE check_value(max_count INTEGER) RETURNS VARCHAR AS 'DECLARE outcome VARCHAR; BEGIN IF (max_count > 2) THEN outcome := ''many''; ELSE outcome := ''few''; END IF; RETURN outcome; END'

CREATE PROCEDURE process_with_loop(max_iterations INTEGER) RETURNS OBJECT AS 'DECLARE counter INTEGER := 0; outcome OBJECT; BEGIN WHILE (counter < 10) DO counter := counter + 1; END WHILE; outcome := OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(''count'', counter, ''status'', ''completed''); RETURN outcome; END'
